title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector Lifesaving Humanitarian Assistance for People Affected by Critical Malnutrition and Education needs in Diga and Kiramu Woredas of East Wollega Zone in Oromia Region, Ethiopia.

description.narrative: ltpgtIn accordance with the 2025 EHF standard allocation FIDO with its partners proposed integrated multisector lifesaving humanitarian assistance project for people affected by malnutrition in Diga and Kiramu Woredas of East Wollega Zone, Oromia Region, Ethiopia. The project will be implemented in 12 months. The proposed total project budget is a $ 1000,000. FIDO will directly implement the Health, Nutrition, WASH and Education component of the project while sub granting the Agriculture to HEKS and ECDD for inclusive programming. ltbrgtFIDO will ensure strong integration and coordination among sectors and implementing partners to maximize the impact and avoid duplication and fragmentation of efforts. The project will ensure synergy and complementarity between and among intervention sectors and partners in order to achieve the maximum possible outcome with limited resources. Acute malnutrition will be an entry point for assistance, with nutrition as the core pillar for integration. Conflict-affected households with acutely malnourished members will be prioritized for other humanitarian aid, if eligible. ltbrgtFIDO will implement the Health, Nutrition, WASH and Education components and implement the agriculture component through its partner- HEKS.ltbrgtThe health component: Will deploy one MHNT for primary healthcare, provide essential drugs, conduct Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), support disease outbreak responses, build healthcare provider capacity, and support vaccination campaigns, rehabilitate health facilities, restore services and support data quality. These interventions increase access to primary healthcare, which improves access to CMAM services and overall nutritional outcomes by addressing disease conditions that cause malnutrition.ltbrgtThe nutrition component: conduct nutrition screening, manage severe acute malnutrition (SAM) cases, provide CMAM capacity building training, supply food for caretakers of SAM cases admitted to SCs, SBCC and FMUAC sessions, offer logistic support and will rehabilitate damaged Stabilization Centre (SC) and Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) sites. This increases access to CMAM services, leading to better nutritional outcomes and improved health, as malnutrition exacerbates various disease conditions.ltbrgtThe WASH intervention: includes solarization of water points, water quality testing, WASH/Non-Food Item (NFI) distribution, and promotion of hygiene and sanitation. These activities contribute to increased access to clean and safe water, reducing communicable diseases and improving health and nutrition outcomes. Institution based WASH facilities construction will enhance infection prevention and control in health centers, reducing cross-infection risks and improving the quality of primary healthcare and nutrition services.ltbrgtThe agriculture component of the project, which will be implemented by HEKS/EPER, include providing improved, locally adapted, drought-tolerant crop (cereals, pulses, vegetables) and fodder seeds, essential farm tools and equipment, and income-generating activities for vulnerable farming and pastoral households. The agriculture intervention connects the emergency relief with the long-term solution. ltbrgtFIDO also collaborates with the Ethiopian Centre for Disability Development (ECDD) to integrate practical disability inclusive interventions such as capacity building, distribution of assistive devices, accessibility audits for all sectors. The project will uphold the EHF Directive on Cross-Cutting Issues, emphasizing PSEA, AAP, Age and Disability Inclusion, and Gender in Humanitarian action. FIDO prioritizes cross-cutting issues, demonstrating strong integration of sectors and sensitivity to protection, gender equality, disability inclusion, RCCE, and vulnerability.lt/pgtltpgtThe education sector intervention will provide scholastic materials and assistive device for those most in need of the support and construct temporary learning spaces (TLS).ltbrgtlt/pgt
